saying: Commenters overwhelmingly ask FDA to spell out concrete dependency controls: pinning to a version-identified model endpoint, contractual advance change notice and deprecation windows, technical detection through fingerprints, canary and shadow testing, regression re-benchmarking, quarantine and rollback, with the manufacturer accountable for device behavior when upstream models change. Several would tier such changes within a PCCP.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on how binding pinning and notice should be: some would make a pinned, version-identified endpoint with contractual change notice a design-control expectation whose absence is a design deficiency, while others frame pinning or equivalent controls as applying where technically and contractually feasible, seeking sufficient information rather than full visibility or control.

sides.summary: Pinning and advance change notice should be mandatory expectations, with absence treated as a design deficiency or higher evidence burden.
Pinning or equivalent change-detection controls should apply where feasible; the goal is enough information and device-level controls to detect and respond, not full control of the model.
